title: Setting up creep feeding for piglets
subtitle: Creep feed builds gut development before weaning. The creep design keeps the sow out of it.
excerpt: Piglets begin exploring solid food at around ten days old. Getting a high-quality creep feed in front of them at this stage, while they are still on the sow, starts the gut flora developing and makes the weaning transition smoother. The creep area must exclude the sow, she will eat everything in it if she can reach.
sourceNotes: AHDB Pork, piglet management factsheets. DEFRA Codes of Recommendations for the Welfare of Pigs, breeding and weaning section. John Seymour, The New Complete Book of Self-Sufficiency (2003), chapter on breeding pigs.

glossaryTerms.definition: A section of the farrowing pen made accessible only to piglets, typically by a gap or step that the sow cannot pass through. Used to provide supplementary feed, heat, and bedding exclusively to the piglets.
A highly palatable, high-protein pellet or cake designed for piglets still nursing. It introduces solid feed gradually before weaning and stimulates gut enzyme development.
A pen designed for a sow to give birth and raise her litter in for the first 3–4 weeks. It typically includes a farrowing rail or crate to reduce piglet crushing, plus a heated area for the piglets.

content.text: Piglets start sniffing and mouthing anything near the sow's snout within the first week of life. By day 10, they follow her to the feeder and try to eat. This is the window to get
in front of them: their gut is starting to develop the enzymes needed for solid food, and a good introduction before weaning cuts post-weaning growth checks significantly.

accessible only to piglets. In a simple outdoor setup: two boards fixed to the pen walls with a gap at floor level of 15-20 cm, large enough for a two-week-old piglet to walk through, small enough that the sow cannot step in. In a purpose-built farrowing house, a raised creep mat behind a low step serves the same purpose.

Place a heat lamp over the creep area pointing down. Piglets chilled away from the sow will not use the feeder. Target floor temperature 30-32°C at the creep surface for the first two weeks, dropping to 28°C by week four.
Place a small flat tray or purpose-made creep feeder inside the creep area. Creep trays visible at floor level attract piglets more reliably than high-sided feeders.
Offer a pinch of creep pellets from day 10. Piglets will not eat a significant amount at first, you are building recognition and habit, not providing nutrition yet.

Creep feed must be fresh. Piglets are more sensitive than older pigs to stale or mouldy feed, and a tray of feed sitting in a warm pen for more than 24 hours will be rejected. Put out small amounts twice a day, what 10 piglets can eat in 20 minutes, rather than filling a feeder once a day.

By week three the litter should be eating 50-100 g per piglet per day. By weaning at 3-4 weeks they should be eating 200-300 g per day without prompting. A litter that is not eating consistently by day 21 needs the creep design reconsidered, usually the feed is too stale, the feeder is too deep for young piglets to reach, or there is insufficient heat.

At weaning, continue with the same creep feed for one week, then transition gradually to weaner pellets over a further week. Changing both the housing and the diet simultaneously increases post-weaning stress. Keep one variable stable.
